sections.text: In that vision Arjuna saw the universe, with its manifold shapes, all embraced in One, its Supreme Lord.
Thereupon Arjuna, dumb with awe, his hair on end, his head bowed, his hands clasped in salutation, addressed the Lord thus:
Arjuna said: O almighty God! I see in Thee the powers of Nature, the various creatures of the world, the Progenitor on his lotus throne, the Sages and the shining angels.

We had been discussing Chapter 11, Vishwarupadarsha yoga of Cosmic Form. So far we have seen in Bhagavad Gita that the quest for each individual is to understand who Bhagavan is. We try in different ways to conceptualize Bhagavan.
And we typically hear that people want to see Bhagavan as a person. But all philosophers basically tell us Bhagavan is not a person -- hes not a man, hes not a woman, hes not it, hes not he, hes not she. So how one can conceptualize Bhagavan is a riddle.
If you see the Abrahamic religions, they forbid any picture of God. What God looks like is not possible to depict. Therefore they say, do not draw.
Do not create an image which can falsify the image of God in your mind. Our religion, on the other hand, makes a very daring attempt to describe Bhagavan. So chapter 11, by Bhagavan Ved Vyas, is a great attempt to describe what Bhagavan would look like if you ever have his darshan.
So far we have seen that Arjuna said: I have understood everything you have said -- that Aham Aksaram Brahma Paramam, I am that imperishable being, I am the source of things and beings. I have no doubt. He said Etat Atha -- that means, so be it.
I understood, no question about it. Im convinced that this is what your nature is, that you are the source of all beings. But how do I contemplate upon you? How do I meditate upon you? Because you told me: meditate on myself, and you will become myself.
So Bhagavan Ved Vyas takes us on Arjunas journey and asks, how does he see it? Arjuna makes a request, and Bhagavan grants it and says, okay, I will show you my total form that nobody has seen before. But you wont be able to see it with your natural vision. I have to give you a divine vision.
Ill give you a divine perspective. With your perspective today, you will not be able to understand this. The things themselves dont change -- but when we change our perspective, we see things in a very different light.
Things we have only seen from one narrow perspective suddenly look different. So right now we are seeing the world from our narrow perspective of I, the limited being. Then conceptualize what would be that greater self.
We are part of the plurality. We want to experience singularity. Bhagavan Krishna told Arjuna, I will change your vision.
And Bhagavan Bedya has already given that divine vision to Sanjaya. Sanjaya can see everything that is happening on Kurukshetra. And whatever Arjuna sees, he sees too.
So Sanjaya saw the form and described it to Dhritarashtra, as we have seen in the last few verses. He confirmed: yes, Krishna granted this vision to Arjuna. He said Anek Vaktra Nayanam, Anek Adbhut Darshanam, Aneka Divya Abharanam.
Everything I see in my world is included in it. I see various types of dresses, various types of ornaments, various types of fragrances. All that he is saying is Anek vaktra Nayanam.
As we have discussed last time, if I take the concept of space out of my mind by some magic, then everything will lump into one. All hands will be of that one big body of a person. And all hands are his, all mouths are his, all eyes are his.
Because now Im seeing it from my worlds perspective. We always see things from our own perspective. We see things based on what we already know.
So if I have to describe something which you have not seen before, I can only describe it from the perspective of what you already know. Do you know where Short Pump is? I dont know where Short Pump is. Do you know where that Walmart is? Okay, well, thats Short Pump.
You need a reference point you already know to get you to Walmart, and then you can put together in your mind what that place should look like. So now, as Bhagavan is giving Arjuna this vision, Sanjaya is putting together in his mind what he has seen in his world: many mouths, many hands, many different types of dresses, many different types of fragrances. Aneka Divya Abharanam.
Then he says, Divya, Mallya, Ambar, Dharam, same thing. Whatever I have seen in my world, I Now see in that form and Sarva ascharimayam Devammanantam everything is very wonderful and infinite. I cannot describe what it is from our perspective.
When we try to put together things in one vision, it looks really infinite. We try to find out how wide this universe is. We have to simply say its infinite.
Because we cant really imagine it. We see the stars, we see the moon. But what is the nature of the cosmic infinite, Anant? Now, if I really take my gaze from my world to the outer world, then he says what you see is Yadibaha Divi Surya Sahasrasya Bhavet Yukpat Uthita.
In my world, I see one sun rising every morning, and I know the splendor of that sun. That splendor is incomparable. In my world, theres nothing I can compare to the suns splendor.
When we design light, designing a surgery room, we have to mimic the sunlight. So you have to come close to the sunlight from your artificial light. You are still only talking about the sunlight.
As we experience this far away from sun. But to experience the sun where it is and to look at it directly -- its splendid. We can hardly look at it.
Now imagine that all the space between all the stars is removed, and all the stars, all the suns in this cosmos, all come together. The splendor of that entity -- all the thousands of stars together! We can look at the sky and look at the stars because theyre so far away. By the time the light comes to us, its so feeble that they look like twinkling stars.
But if they all come together -- because you have removed space and time from your mind -- they all come together at the same time. Therefore, Divi Surya Sahasrasya Yadi Bhaha: if thousands of suns were rising in the sky, if you can imagine that -- Sadrushi Sat Bhasah Tasya Mahatmanaha -- even that cannot describe the splendor of that great being, that Mahatma. Because he is the stars, he is the moon, he is everything that we can think of.
Therefore, we cannot draw his picture. Because everything that I can imagine as part of this cosmos, Bhagavan said, it is me. Then this is my Eightfold prakriti that includes everything they can think of.
Bhoomi apah analaha kam vayuhu mana buddhi ahanka. So space is part of that manifestation, everything else I can imagine. Now, if I say that I have Bhagavans darshan, all that darshan has to come together in one.
Therefore it is not possible. But what we try to do as human beings, we personify that reason in one person. So therefore he said, bhagavan, Im seeing this vision in your body.
Even in our life, what we do is all the divinity that we can think of or we have imagined of. We assign that to one person. We want to see that in one person.
So therefore we say, bhagavan, I see all that in Chinbananda somebody says, I saw all that in Bhagavan Rajneesh, somebody says, because we gather all that conceptualization of divinity into one person, we want to see that in one person. And then we get disappointed because a person by very nature cannot have all the attributes of that entire divinity. But if we change our perspective, then we will be able to see that.
So Bhagavan said, yadibaha divi Surya Sahastrasya Bhavet yukpat Uthita Sadrushi saa saad Bhasah Tasya mahat manah. Splendor of that being which represents totality, heirs of thousands of sons. You cannot describe it.
Tatra Ekastam, Jagat Krishnam, Pravibhaktam, Anekata, its all centered into one. Because thats what Arjuna asked for. I want to see all that centered into you, all in one.
Right now I see them as Pravibhakta, different parts. I know this cosmos exist as nature, as Lords manifestation, but in different parts I can manage. I can manage to understand.
It is your world, his world, her world, my planet, different planets. There are different parts of his manifestation. From my narrow perspective, I can understand it.
But now he says, Tatra Ekastam is centered into one Jagat Krushnam. The entire Jagat Jagat includes everything. Jagat includes your physical cosmos as well as your emotional cosmos and your intellectual cosmos.
Everything that you can think of that the greatness of our Hinduism, it has included in Astra, Prakriti, mind, intellect and ego. Without that, your world is not complete. If I can put all this together, one person and what that vision would be, thats what Arjuna is seeing right now.
In that Mahatma Deva Devashya Sari re. Arjuna saw in the body of the God of Gods. Krishna is no longer a person.
Dhritarashtra can relate to who he knew as the king of Yadavas or Pandavas ally. But now he says hes a Deva Devasya, the God of all the gods. So he said, I see the Maruta and I see Rudras, all these Devas, all the deities which he is the God of all those deities.
Everything that we have imagined, who has the control over this world, he has control over all of them. Deva Deveshary, Pandavahatada, Pandava Arjuna. Arjuna saw in the body of that God of gods this splendor of thousands of suns blazing at the same time.
So what could be the reaction of Arjuna Vishma Yavista overcame by the wonderment? Hes completely dumbfounded. Rustiroma is here standing on hands. I dont know if the English translation of in our language its very well used.
Goosebumps is the only thing come to my mind in English. Hes having goosebumps. Hes completely dumbfounded looking at this.
He asked for it, but did not know what to expect. Now hes seeing in the body of the God of God because hes all that vision is personified in one person. Ristiroma Dhananjaya Dhananjaya again Arjuna Pranasya Silasadvam.
Once you have that experience, as soon as you see him, Chamatkar I may not believe anything about when he does Chamatkar, he takes out a Rolex watch and gives you namaskar right there. So Pranamya Sirasadevam, as soon as he realized the nature of this total being is surrendered. We dont surrender right now because we dont think this is all true, even though we kind of learn and all that.
But when it comes to our life, we say, no, no, I have better control. I have people come to me and say, stop coming to class. I think it was actually giving him less motivation to do things.
So right now our motivation in working in a world is we dont have much trust in him. We dont think he can take care of it. I really need to look out for myself, look out for number one.
That used to be a mantra when I came to this country. Somebody has started and said, think about number one. Number one is you start from thinking about you first, then comes everybody else.
Your family, your children, your. Start from you take care of yourself first and then go to. But here he said he realized that he is nobody with whom he is relating to what he is seeing Nobody.
So Pranaam is Sirasa Devam Dandavat Pranam Only the South Indians do that Dandavat Pranayama Punjabi is doing Mathotic they just put the head on and Gujaratvi yeah Pranamya Sirasadevam, Once you have understood the greatness of who you are relating to, you are completely surrendered to him.

In these verses, Arjuna sees the entire universe with its manifold forms all embraced in One - the supreme Lord. His response is immediate and visceral: dumb with awe, hair standing on end, head bowed, hands clasped in salutation. He sees all the powers of Nature, the various creatures, the Progenitor Brahma on his lotus throne, the Sages, and the shining angels. Notice the dramatic shift: the moment Arjuna truly perceives Krishnas nature, spontaneous surrender arises. He does not decide to bow; bowing happens naturally.
This points to why we do not surrender in daily life - we have not truly seen. We may intellectually accept spiritual teachings, but when push comes to shove, we still believe we have better control, that we need to look out for number one. Arjunas goosebumps and spontaneous prostration show what happens when intellectual understanding becomes direct perception. The teaching suggests that true surrender is not an act of will but a natural response to genuine recognition of the divine.
Reflect today on your relationship with surrender. When you say Thy will be done or I trust the universe, is it genuine recognition or merely words? Notice the situations where you grip tightly, trying to control outcomes. Ask yourself: What would I need to truly see for surrender to arise spontaneously? Consider that perhaps you are not lacking in willingness to surrender but in the clarity of perception that makes surrender the obvious and natural response. Practice today by consciously acknowledging your limitations in even small matters - traffic, weather, others moods - and notice if a sense of release naturally follows this honest recognition.
